sections.label: White Paper on Women's Development
sections.summary: A first-ever White Paper on Singapore Women's Development has been put together and Parliament will debate it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In response, we have put together the first-ever White Paper on Singapore Women's Development, which Parliament will now debate.

sections.label: 1961 Women's Charter
sections.summary: The new PAP Government passed the Women's Charter in 1961, institutionalising rights and responsibilities in marriage and protecting women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: On assuming office, almost the first thing the new PAP Government did was to pass the Women's Charter in 1961.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Charter institutionalised the rights and responsibilities of men and women in marriage and ensured the protection and welfare of women in Singapore.

sections.label: Gender pay gap narrowed
sections.summary: The adjusted gender pay gap halved to around 4% over two decades, and women CEOs remain a minority but exceed the global average.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Our adjusted gender pay gap has further narrowed, halving to around 4% over two decades.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Among chief executive officers, women remain a minority, but we are encouraged that Singapore has more than double the global average.

sections.label: Women's life expectancy 2020
sections.summary: By 2020, Singapore women's life expectancy reached 86, surpassed only by Switzerland and Japan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: By 2020, Singapore women's life expectancy had reached 86, surpassed only by two countries – Switzerland and Japan.

sections.label: Women's Charter 60th anniversary
sections.summary: Last year was the 60th anniversary of the Women's Charter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Last year was the 60th anniversary of the Women's Charter.

sections.label: White Paper call to action
sections.summary: The White Paper is a call for all to act, and notes women's parliamentary seats rose from two of 64 to 30 of 103.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: While many Singapore women are empowered by caregiver support, some will continue to be constrained by cultural preferences held by society and even themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Therefore, more than being a comprehensive plan of action by the Government, the White Paper is a clarion call for each and every one to take action – take action in our homes, our workplaces, our community, our relationships; take action to recognise women's achievements as society's achievements; take action to pursue women's progress as part of society's progress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In December 1965, when the Parliament of Independent Singapore first sat, there were only two active women out of 64 Members.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, women occupy 30 out 103 seats, a nine-fold increase in percentage terms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Just as our predecessors have laid the foundations for women to succeed, we, too, must build new scaffoldings for future generations of women to thrive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This White Paper reaffirms our shared vision of a fairer and more inclusive society.

sections.label: Call for fullest attention
sections.summary: The speaker calls on everyone to give it our fullest attention and support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For this reason, I call on everyone to give it our fullest attention and support.

sections.label: First FSC formation
sections.summary: Syn Neo spearheaded the formation of the first FSC in 1978 in the then-Ministry of Social Affairs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Syn Neo spearheaded the formation of the very first FSC in 1978 in the then-Ministry of Social Affairs.

sections.label: Conversations on Singapore Women's Development
sections.summary: The speaker cites Singapore's education record and describes launching year-long Conversations on Singapore Women's Development, with 160 Conversations and nearly 6,000 participants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: When I shared that, in Singapore, less than 1% of our children did not complete 10 years of education, and that our girls were free to choose their own education pathways, including STEM, the room fell silent – I think in disbelief – that we have achieved both of these.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: But we should now move from quantitative achievements to one where the quality of development is our focus, which is why we launched the year-long nationwide Conversations on Singapore Women’s Development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We pressed ahead, even amid the pandemic, and organised 160 Conversations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Nearly 6,000 participants, representing wide segments of society, responded to the call and joined us, sharing with us their hopes and aspirations of our women.

sections.label: Women in leadership roles
sections.summary: More women in leadership helps governance and stewardship, with women's board participation almost 20% in Top 100 listed companies and reaching 30% in Statutory Boards and Top 100 IPCs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Having more women in leadership roles helps to catalyse robust governance and better stewardship of organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am glad that women’s participation on Singapore boards is almost 20% in Top 100 listed companies and reaching 30% in Statutory Boards and Top 100 IPCs today.

sections.label: Preschool places by 2025
sections.summary: By around 2025, eight in 10 Singaporean children can have a place in a Government-supported preschool.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: By around 2025, eight in 10 Singaporean children can have a place in a Government-supported preschool.

sections.label: Garden honouring Singapore women
sections.summary: The Government will dedicate Dhoby Ghaut Green as a public garden honouring Singapore women, and the Prime Minister will launch a travelling exhibition on 22 April.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: At the closing session of the Conversations, the Prime Minister had announced that the Government had taken on board a proposal from the Singapore Council of Women's Organisations (SCWO) and will dedicate a public garden to honour, celebrate and recognise the contributions of Singapore women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that we have identified Dhoby Ghaut Green, which is located in the heart of the city, for the garden.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister will also launch a travelling "Celebrating Singapore Women" exhibition on 22 April.

sections.label: White Paper decade-long plan
sections.summary: The White Paper begins a decade of work by MSF, the Government and partners to build respect between men and women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: (In English): To conclude, the White Paper is just the start of a decade of work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: There will be many more conversations and action plans to come.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: It is a decade-long plan of action and commitment by MSF, the Government and key partners, which we will carry to fruition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will build a culture of respect and partnership between men and women and across all spheres of society.

sections.label: Welcoming White Paper recommendations
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the 25 far-reaching recommendations made in the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With this, I welcome the 25 very far-reaching recommendations made in the White Paper.

sections.label: Labour Movement on FWAs
sections.summary: The Labour Movement has piloted place and train programmes and supports the White Paper's recommendations on flexible work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Together with the Labour Movement's ecosystem partners, we have started the process of refreshing and professionalising such occupations and have piloted place and train programmes in these sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement recognises that our Singaporean women often play the role as the primary caregiver in our families and thus have been advocating since the 1990s on flexible work arrangements (FWAs) as a workplace norm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We welcome and support the White Paper's recommendations on FWAs.

sections.label: Mentorships for women re-entering work
sections.summary: The Labour Movement welcomes the White Paper's recommendations on using mentorships to augment opportunities for women re-entering the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement welcomes the White Paper's recommendations on using mentorships to augment opportunities for women to re-enter the workplace.

sections.label: NTUC protecting SME workers
sections.summary: NTUC engages employers and provides shared HR resources to prevent workplace discrimination and protect whistle-blowers within reason.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The NTUC has, hence, started to look to channel efforts into enhancing the protection of SME workers by engaging our employers in dialogues, talks and webinars, whilst providing shared HR resources that work to prevent workplace discrimination and to protect whistle-blowers within reason.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We are committed to equipping our SMEs and companies with better standard operating procedures (SOPs) that can help to create discrimination- and harassment-free workplaces.

sections.label: PME Task Force workplace fairness
sections.summary: The 2021 PME Task Force called for stronger enforcement against unfair practices and safe whistle-blowing policies to combat workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: More recently, in 2021, the PME Task Force driven by NTUC and Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF) called for strengthening enforcement against errant companies adopting unfair practices, such as by empowering TAFEP to impose penalties on recalcitrant companies and putting in place safe whistle-blowing policies and procedures to combat discrimination in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we look forward to proposals by the Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness at the end of 2022, we will continue to safeguard the safety of women workers and help employers create a work environment that is free from discrimination and harassment.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements guidelines
sections.summary: The Government committed to entrenching flexible work arrangements as a workplace norm and to introduce new Tripartite Guidelines by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 pandemic has shown us that it is possible for some categories of workers to telecommute full-time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, heartened that the Government has committed to entrenching FWAs as a workplace norm and to introduce new Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs by 2024 to ensure that employers consider FWA requests fairly and properly.

sections.label: Jobs Closer to Home programme
sections.summary: In Radin Mas, the Singapore Manufacturing Federation was partnered to launch the Jobs Closer to Home programme in 2021 for women with caregiving responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In Radin Mas, we partnered the Singapore Manufacturing Federation to launch the Jobs Closer to Home programme in 2021, to help women with caregiving responsibilities find jobs that are within five kilometres of the constituency, or a few bus stops away from home.

sections.label: Women in global roles
sections.summary: A PWC survey found 71% of millennial women aspire to global roles, while Mercer found only 20% of global expatriates are women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to a survey conducted by PWC, 71% of millennial women aspire to take on a global role.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, Mercer's 2020 Worldwide Survey on International Assignment Policies and Practices found that only 20% of the global expatriate workforce is made up of women.

sections.label: Mentoring women and fair employment
sections.summary: FWA mentors support younger women, and MOM is enshrining the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices into legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: FWA has a deep pool of successful women in the financial industry who contribute their time by mentoring younger women in the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Many of FWA's mentors have gone through overseas stints and their mentees are able to approach them for advice on how to overcome challenges and flourish from such opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I hope that with EDB's support, more professional associations and industry partners will create such mentorship programmes to help our millennial women professionals go global.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: MOM is in the process of enshrining the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TGFEP) into legislation and I hope that the Act will state unequivocally that employers cannot penalise female employees or reject a perfectly qualified jobseeker simply based on pregnancy.

sections.label: Women in SAF service
sections.summary: The percentage of total women service personnel in the SAF is only about 7%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The percentage of the total women service personnel in the SAF is only about 7%.

sections.label: Women in Singapore Police
sections.summary: From 10 Policewomen in 1949, women now make up 19%, of which 16% are in senior leadership roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: From just 10 Policewomen in 1949 to 19%, of which 16% are in senior leadership roles.

sections.label: Women in STEM industries
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with the White Paper's recommendation to support women in STEM, noting women are only 3% of aviation chief executives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am in agreement with the White Paper's recommendation to encourage and support women to choose and excel in science, technology, engineering, mathematics (STEM) industries, which have been predominantly male, until recent years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am currently employed in the aviation sector and women make up only 3% of chief executives, compared with more than 10% in many other industries.

sections.label: STEM graduates career pursuit
sections.summary: Only 55% of women STEM graduates pursued related careers, compared to 70% of men.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Only 55% of the women who graduated with STEM degrees or diplomas pursued related careers, compared to 70% of men.

sections.label: Pioneering female police officer
sections.summary: Mdm Zuraidah Abdullah joined the SPF in 1986 and was the first woman to become Senior Assistant Commissioner of Police.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One pioneering female officer in the Police force is Mdm Zuraidah Abdullah.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: She joined the SPF in 1986, helmed several command positions in operations and training and was the first woman to achieve the rank of Senior Assistant Commissioner of Police.

sections.label: Women at Tokyo Olympics
sections.summary: At the Tokyo Olympics, 17 of Singapore's 23 athletes were women, and six of 10 Paralympics competitors were female.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At the recent Tokyo Olympics, out of our 23 national athletes fielded, 17 were women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Similarly, of the 10 competitors for the Paralympics, there were six female representatives.

sections.label: Migrant domestic workers numbers
sections.summary: As of 2020, there are almost 250,000 migrant domestic workers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As of 2020, there are almost 250,000 migrant domestic workers in Singapore.

sections.label: Sabbaticals and women representation
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for sabbatical incentives for both genders and more women in the Cabinet, beyond three women and 17 male Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At a certain phase, they may have to prioritise familial responsibilities, like caregiving for young children or aged parents and take a break from their jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I trust that the Government will consider providing incentives to encourage MNCs, and especially SMEs, to introduce a sabbatical system not just for women but for both genders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Women, actually, do care about the men's welfare as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am confident that the recommendations will drive significant improvements in the decades ahead and enable more women in Singapore to hold up half the sky, while the men hold up the other half.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On a personal note, as we chart our new way forward together, I hope to see more women representation in the Cabinet with more than just a mere 15% made up of only three women and 17 male Ministers.

sections.label: Workers' Party supports White Paper
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports the spirit of the Motion and the White Paper's goal of a fairer, more inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party supports the spirit of the Motion and the White Paper's overarching goal of achieving a fairer and more inclusive society.

sections.label: Gender pay gap rates
sections.summary: The White Paper states the adjusted rate dropped to 4.3% in 2020, with the unadjusted median gender pay gap at 14.4%.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The White Paper mentions that the adjusted rate has dropped further to 4.3% in 2020, with the unadjusted median gender pay gap being 14.4%.

sections.label: Call for pay gap reporting
sections.summary: The speaker repeats the manifesto call for employers with 10 or more employees to report gender pay gap to MOM.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This does not give us a good picture of the problem.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We, therefore, repeat the call from our manifesto that employers with 10 or more employees should be required to report to MOM the gender pay gap for the same job description.

sections.label: New York City pink tax study
sections.summary: A 2015 New York City study found women's products cost 7% more and women paid more in every industry studied.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A study commissioned in 2015 by New York City found that women's products cost 7% more than similar products for men and that women paid more in every industry studied.

sections.label: Women's unpaid labour burden
sections.summary: Women bear a disproportionate share of unpaid labour, including the invisible mental load of overseeing households.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Women also bear a disproportionate share of unpaid labour, both tangible and "invisible" in the form of the mental load, because it is still usually the woman who is expected to oversee the smooth running of our households.

sections.label: Anti-discrimination legislation welcomed
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes anti-discrimination legislation, a 2020 manifesto proposal, noting discrimination persists despite TAFEP guidance.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Turning to anti-discrimination legislation, I am happy to hear that anti-discrimination legislation will be introduced in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This move has long been called for by Members in this House and, indeed, is one of the proposals contained in our 2020 manifesto, where we called for anti-discrimination legislation to be formally instituted to prohibit against employment discrimination on the basis of race, gender, age and against Singapore Citizens.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It would also give our businesses clarity to know what discriminatory practices are, and to introduce internal processes to protect their employees from discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is also notable that discrimination and discriminatory practices persist despite the guidance and counselling offered through the Tripartite Alliance for Fair Employment Practices (TAFEP).

sections.label: Maternal health and well-being strategy
sections.summary: A cousin's comment that motherhood is harder than summiting Mount Everest is cited to argue for a child and maternal health and well-being strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One such conversation which shall always remain with me is a comment made by a cousin that she found being a mother was actually harder than summiting Mount Everest!

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This difficulty is why the development of a child and maternal health and well-being strategy is so important if we are to support women in their motherhood journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our focus must move beyond just medical care.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is good to see that efforts announced during the Committee of Supply (COS) this year will provide care for maternal mental health and to encourage support for them at the workplace and in the community.

sections.label: Panel on women's health
sections.summary: A panel led by Senior Minister of State Amy Khor to advise HPB on women's health was set up in 2012.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, I note that a panel led by Senior Minister of State Amy Khor to advise HPB on women's health was set up in 2012 and that work has been done to promote women's health.

sections.label: Challenging gender stereotypes in education
sections.summary: The speaker says curriculum and education must go beyond planned Character Citizenship Education changes to challenge gender stereotypes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Before I close, I would like to make one final point about the deep mindset shifts required of us and the comprehensive societal education necessary to bring about much-needed change.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We have to go beyond the planned Character Citizenship Education (CCE) changes to ensure that our curriculum and education, in general, make a conscious effort to challenge gender stereotypes.

sections.label: Hokkien saying and Motion support
sections.summary: The speaker quotes a Hokkien saying about having a good heart and thinking and saying good things, and supports the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Hokkien, "have a good heart, think good things, say good things." I support the Motion.

sections.label: Women in STEM in Singapore
sections.summary: Women in Singapore's STEM sector increased to 32.4% in 2020, which is lower than in other sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In Singapore, while the number of women in the Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) sector has increased to 32.4% in 2020, it is lower in comparison to other sectors.

sections.label: Job vacancies unfilled over six months
sections.summary: Job vacancies left unfilled for more than six months increased by 8%, to 35%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Job vacancies left unfilled for more than six months increased by 8%, to 35%.

sections.label: Tripartite Guidelines on FWA requests
sections.summary: The White Paper states MOM will work with tripartite partners on new Tripartite Guidelines by 2024 requiring employers to fairly consider FWA requests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The White Paper outlines that MOM will work with the tripartite partners to put in place a new set of Tripartite Guidelines by 2024, requiring employers to fairly and properly consider FWA requests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: My question is: why wait till 2024 to introduce the new set of Tripartite Guidelines?

sections.label: SMEs need support for FWAs
sections.summary: SMEs can benefit more from FWAs but need more support than larger organisations due to lean HR teams and transition demands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: SMEs can also benefit from FWAs and, actually, they stand to benefit more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But, as we advocate for FWAs, we must recognise that, for SMEs, they will require more support than larger organisations in the implementation of FWAs, as they have very lean HR teams and they may not have the capacity and there will be a lot of transition and transformation.

sections.label: Purpose of maternity leave
sections.summary: Maternity leave allows women time to care and bond with their newborn and to rest and recover from pregnancy and childbirth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While the purpose of maternity leave is to allow women time to care and bond with their newborn child, let us not forget that maternity leave is also to allow time for women to rest and recover from the physical changes and strains that she went through in the nine months of pregnancy, as well as childbirth.

sections.label: Mindset shifts for fair society
sections.summary: The White Paper states realising a fair and inclusive society requires mindset shifts from everyone, as it is about all of us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: To realise the aspirations of enabling a fair and inclusive society for both women and men to achieve our fullest potential and progress together, we must recognise the need to make the mindset shifts, each and every one of us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: One of the important points of this White Paper is that it is about all of us and not just about some of us.

sections.label: Poll on gender-based online harms
sections.summary: A Sunlight AfA sensing poll found 31% of respondents personally experienced or witnessed gender-based online harms, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Based on a sensing poll conducted by the Sunlight AfA, 31% of respondents have either personally experienced or witnessed gender-based online harms or both.

sections.label: POHA amendment outlawing doxxing
sections.summary: In 2019, the Protection from Harassment Act was amended to outlaw doxxing, addressing harassment the woman journalist had endured.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In 2019, the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) was amended to outlaw doxxing, which would address the kind of harassment that the woman journalist had endured.

sections.label: Gallup Global Law and Order ranking
sections.summary: Since 2017, Singapore has been ranked first in Gallup's Global Law and Order report.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Since 2017, we have been ranked first in Gallup's Global Law and Order report.

sections.label: Sunlight AfA online safety poll
sections.summary: The Sunlight AfA sensing poll found 72% of males and 60% of females felt safe from online harms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The sensing poll conducted by the Sunlight AfA found that while 72% of males felt safe from harms while online, only 60% of females did.

sections.label: AfA online harms initiatives
sections.summary: Since July 2021 the AfA surveyed online harms, engaged over 240 parents and youths, launched a resource website, and will roll out more initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Since its launch in July 2021, the AfA has administered a survey to understand the incidence and impact of online harms in Singapore, engaged over 240 parents and youths to raise awareness about online harms and impart tips on how they can help their loved ones navigate the digital space safely, launched a website containing informational resources about online risks and safety tools on technology platforms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: What has been particularly encouraging to the AfA members is that the Government is responding to the calls we have been making, by introducing Codes of Practice for Internet platforms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The AfA will roll out more initiatives in the coming months to empower individuals to recognise online harms and build a more holistic system of support for victims.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: These include a workshop to equip youths to support peers who may be experiencing online harms and a pilot to provide counselling intervention to victims of online harms.

sections.label: PAP Women's Wing online harms toolkit
sections.summary: The PAP Women's Wing adopted tackling online harms as its 2022 International Women's Day theme and rolled out a resource toolkit with lawyers and counsellors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The People's Action Party Women’s Wing adopted the theme of tackling online harms for its International Women's Day activation for 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: It partnered lawyers and counsellors to roll out a resource toolkit to equip branch volunteers to be good listeners and helpful responders when members of the public bring up issues relating to online harms during Meet-the-People Sessions.

sections.label: Roadmap for women's digital safety
sections.summary: The speaker says a roadmap now exists to tackle online harms and close the digital safety gap for Singapore women and girls.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Back then, I felt upset for her, but did not yet have a clear idea of what can be done to tackle such online harms and defend the dignity and confidence of women online.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: I believe we have a roadmap now, which is constantly being expanded and refined, thanks to the partnership and collective wisdom of the women and men who stepped forth to join our AfA, and all those who are committed to uplift digital safety for Singapore women and girls.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The digital safety gap can be closed for our women and girls.

sections.label: Foreign spouses and spousal maintenance rules
sections.summary: The passage proposes transparent time-based rules for foreign spouses with Singaporean children, a points-based immigration regime, and changes to spousal maintenance laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thirdly, transparent time-based structural rules to enable foreign spouses with Singaporean children, who are mostly women, to move towards Permanent Residency (PR) status and citizenship – and extending that point, a more predictable and transparent points-based immigration regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And fourthly, in the spirit of gender equality, changes to our laws on spousal maintenance to be fairer to house-husbands and men who have less income and assets than their wives in the event of a divorce.

sections.label: Workplace sexual harassment and TAFEP
sections.summary: An AWARE report cites a 2020 survey finding two in five Singapore workers experienced workplace sexual harassment, and TAFEP's role appears limited to interceding with employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To cite an AWARE report on gender equality released on 28 July last year, "According to the results of a 2020 Ipsos-AWARE national survey, two in five workers in Singapore have experienced workplace sexual harassment in the past five years, including being on the receiving end of crude sexual and sexist remarks and being touched physically in ways that made them feel distress or alarm." So, this is not an insignificant problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Victims of sexual harassment can go to Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) but the role of TAFEP, currently, would appear to be limited to interceding with the victim's employer to put in place better anti-sexual harassment policies and to deploy its own disciplinary and internal dispute handling procedures as a company.

sections.label: Malaysia sexual harassment law
sections.summary: Malaysia amended its Employment Act in 2014 to define and criminalise sexual harassment as unwanted conduct of a sexual nature that is offensive, humiliating or threatening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Malaysia amended its Employment Act to specifically define and criminalise acts of sexual harassment in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Malaysian law defines sexual harassment as "any unwanted conduct of a sexual nature, whether verbal, nonverbal, visual, gestural or physical, directed at a person, which is offensive, humiliating or a threat to their wellbeing".

sections.label: Migrant spouses residency data
sections.summary: An AWARE report cites data that from 2012 to 2016, 13,900 migrant spouses of Singapore Citizens received LTVP out of 16,600 applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To quote from the July 2021 AWARE report once again, "the latest publicly available data shows that from 2012 to 2016, 13,900 migrant spouses of Singapore Citizens were granted LTVP out of 16,600 applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A national study on cross-national families found that 55% of the 655 foreign-born mothers interviewed had attained permanent residency and 26% had become Singapore Citizens after an average of eight years of marriage, but 17% of them still held LTVP or LTVP+.

sections.label: Spouse visa criteria abroad
sections.summary: The passage states UK spouse visa income criteria, German language and citizenship test criteria, and lists countries with points-based immigration systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The criteria for a UK spouse visa, for instance, states that the applicant and spouse must have a combined income of at least £18,600 a year, among other requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Germany, the criteria include specific language proficiency levels in the passing of the citizenship test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: New Zealand, Australia, Canada and the UK are examples of countries with transparent criteria and a points-based immigration system.

sections.label: Maintenance order for retiree
sections.summary: A 2014 media report cited in the House described a man ordered to pay $70,000 in maintenance despite being a retiree earning less than his ex-wife.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The example was cited in this House of a 2014 media report on a man who was ordered to pay $70,000 in maintenance despite the fact that he was a retiree, the ex-wife earned more than him and he paid the mortgage for their home.

sections.label: Care work compensation and pregnancy discrimination
sections.summary: The passage states that if recognition and support for care work are expanded, compensation should cover all care work, while noting feedback of employers discriminating against pregnant women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If we agree today that, in principle, we want to expand recognition, legal support and improve autonomy in care work, then, in the name of fairness, we must ensure that this is also so when things go poorly, that we provide a route for compensation for all care work, be it the contributions of men and non-citizen women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, we must also acknowledge that we continue to receive feedback that there are employers, large and small, who discriminate against women who are pregnant.

sections.label: Legislation for flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government would legislate flexible work arrangements, such as early release for staff with children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Government look into having legislation to enshrine FWAs, such as early release of staff with children, so that they could pick up their children from childcare or spend more quality family time?

sections.label: Enticing companies to implement FWAs
sections.summary: The passage suggests the Government entice companies implementing FWAs with privileges like a higher foreign worker quota or Workfare co-payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To nudge hesitant employers and companies, I would like to suggest that the Government consider enticing companies that implement FWAs with privileges like a higher foreign worker quota or a co-payment element like Workfare.

sections.label: Subsidy or waiver of maid levy
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry would consider a subsidy to lessen financial burden or waive the maid levy entirely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider some form of subsidy to lessen their financial burden or even waive the maid levy entirely?

sections.label: Married men employed more than women
sections.summary: The passage states that married men are employed 1.3 times more than women.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Married men are employed 1.3 times more than women.

sections.label: White Paper on parental leave weeks
sections.summary: The passage states the White Paper suggests this could amount to up to 22 weeks with the father's eligible share bumped up to eight weeks.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The White Paper suggests that this could amount to up to 22 weeks with the father's eligible share bumped up to eight weeks.

sections.label: Workers' Party shared parental leave scheme
sections.summary: The passage states the Workers' Party manifesto calls for a 24-week shared parental leave scheme with minimum shares for mother and father.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As my friend Sengkang Member of Parliament Louis Chua will note in his speech, the Workers' Party has, in our manifesto, explicitly called for a different shared parental leave scheme of 24 weeks with a minimum of half of this to be granted to the mother, and a sixth to the father.

sections.label: FWAs coverage target report
sections.summary: The report calls for FWAs to cover 40% of employees by end-2022 but gives no similar public sector commitment, only that it will take the lead.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More generally, the report calls for FWAs to be boosted to cover 40% of all employees by the end of 2022 but does not offer any similar commitment for the expansion of coverage of FWAs in the public sector, only stating that the public sector will "take the lead".

sections.label: Gender quotas study findings
sections.summary: Studies found randomly assigned gender quotas in India and mandated board representation in Norway led to later gains for women.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In one study, when gender quotas are randomly assigned – this is the gold standard for causal inference – in village councils in India, the prior exposure to a female leader gives rise to subsequent lasting electoral gains.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In another study, mandated board representation in Norway led to an improved likelihood that women would, subsequently, secure leadership.

sections.label: Limited quota for board seats
sections.summary: A limited quota, like a voluntary one-third target for 10 years applying to largest firms, could be viable given current 18% representation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That is why a limited quota could be a viable way forward.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This would be akin to, say, a voluntary target of a third of board seats being held by women and holding this target for a temporary period of 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It would only apply to the largest firms, thereby minimising the compliance costs for small corporations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And a third seems eminently attainable, given how female representation is currently about 18%; this would amount to a doubling from the present share.

sections.label: Report and public sector role
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Motion but finds the report sanguine about Government's role, noting silence on Civil Service leadership.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To be clear, the report represents a positive step in advancing the cause of true gender equality in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, while I support the Motion, I have found the report to be sanguine in the role that the Government, through the Public Service, can play in ushering in such positive changes in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Charity, surely, begins at home, and the deafening silence on how the demonstration effect of Government leadership by rolling out the proposed actions decisively within the Civil Service strikes me as inexplicable and, honestly, somewhat peculiar.

sections.label: Action 13 family violence protection
sections.summary: Action 13 on enhancing protection for victim-survivors of family violence states the responding team will include social service professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is in particular reference to Action 13 on enhancing protection for victim-survivors of family violence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was stated at page 54 that, moving forward, the team responding to cases of family violence will include social service professionals.

sections.label: Merseyside rapid response initiative
sections.summary: In the 1990s Merseyside police issued neck pendant alarms to victims of repeated high-risk violence for a short period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the 1990s, police in Merseyside innovated with a rapid response initiative to address cases of repeated violence identified as particularly high-risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As research had shown that a repeat incident was most likely to occur within days of the first incident, victims were issued with neck pendant alarms for a short period of time.

sections.label: Agencies innovating preventive strategies
sections.summary: The passage asks whether agencies will innovate their own preventive strategies in particularly serious cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will our agencies be innovating their own preventive strategies in particularly serious cases?

sections.label: Cuomo sexual harassment defence
sections.summary: Andrew Cuomo faced sexual harassment allegations and said he was unaware his touching was offensive, attributing it to his Italian heritage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There was an example of this that made international headlines last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Then-New York Governor, Andrew Cuomo, faced allegations that he had sexually harassed female employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In his defence, he said that he was unaware that his behaviour of touching female employees was offensive and attributed it to his Italian heritage.

sections.label: Gender strategy and data
sections.summary: Examples cited were health and safety standards and safe food, and Enterprise Singapore and the Singapore Standards Council will develop a gender strategy in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Examples cited were minimising workplace accidents with health and safety standards and ensuring food in Singapore was safe for consumption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was stated that Enterprise Singapore and the Singapore Standards Council will develop a new gender strategy in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order to track whether such initiatives are effective, I will make the general point on the need to continually collate and publish data on a gender-aggregated basis.

sections.label: Scheduling milestones for FWAs
sections.summary: The speaker worries organisations will revert to old ways of working and suggests scheduling milestones leading up to the 2024 Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Now that the "burning platform" has less urgency, I worry that organisations will not devote enough time and attention to FWAs and revert to the old ways of working, something which my colleague, Mr Melvin Yong, mentioned in his speech earlier, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, while I understand that the introduction of the Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs will take place only in 2024, we should consider scheduling important milestones that would, eventually, lead up to it.

sections.label: Respite care places added
sections.summary: The passage acknowledges Government efforts adding 3,100 homecare and 4,600 daycare places for seniors since 2015, one in Pasir Ris.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While we continue towards changing the mindset that women should be the primary caregivers, we must continue to improve the support for our caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I acknowledge the Government's efforts to increase the supply of respite care with 3,100 homecare places and 4,600 daycare places for seniors added since 2015, one of which is in Pasir Ris.

sections.label: Doubling Home Caregiving Grant
sections.summary: The passage supports doubling the Home Caregiving Grant from $200 to $400 for lower-income households, which has benefited 31,000 individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Yet, another way we could extend help to reduce caregivers' financial strain is through the enhancement of the Home Caregiving Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I support the doubling of the Home Caregiving Grant from $200 to $400 for lower-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is a significant enhancement to the grant which has already benefited 31,000 individuals.

sections.label: Childcare subsidies and caregiving support
sections.summary: The speaker notes Mdm Neo's Home Caregiving Grant application and asks about subsidies for private childcare and a review of differentiated childcare subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Since our visit to Mdm Neo, I am happy that she is now applying for the Home Caregiving Grant and is our monthly beneficiary at our Pasir Ris Care Store.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Besides subsidies for anchor or partner childcare operators, can the Ministry consider providing subsidies for private schools and private childcare options, such as those in religious organisations that are already available?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I also urge the Government to review the differentiated childcare subsidy of $300 per month for working and $150 per month for non-working mothers.

sections.label: Mother's depression and childcare subsidy
sections.summary: A Pasir Ris mother quit her job while recovering from depression, and the family worried about spending $300 more monthly under the differentiated childcare subsidy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, one of our mothers in Pasir Ris had to quit her job while she recovers from depression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, the family was worried that with the differentiated childcare subsidy, by her not working, they will have to spend $300 more per month, in addition to her losing her income.

sections.label: Muslim women's financial independence aspiration
sections.summary: A PPIS study on the aspirations of Muslim women in Singapore found financial independence is one of their top aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In a study conducted by PPIS on the Aspirations of a Muslim Women in Singapore, one of the top aspirations of Muslim Women is to be financially independent.

sections.label: Paternity leave and financial trade-offs
sections.summary: Two weeks of paid statutory paternity leave, versus the OECD average of 10 weeks, means fathers wanting equal child-rearing responsibility face financial trade-offs such as unpaid leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A mere two weeks of paid statutory paternity leave, compared to the OECD average of 10 weeks, means that even the most well-meaning of fathers who wish to take on a more egalitarian share of the child-rearing responsibility must make direct financial trade-offs, such as via unpaid leave.

sections.label: Shared parental leave scheme proposal
sections.summary: The Workers' Party calls for 24 weeks of Government-paid shared parental leave, with minimum four weeks for fathers and 12 weeks for mothers, replacing existing entitlements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The existing elective four weeks of shared parental leave, whereby mothers have to make the election to share their maternity leave, means that, in practice, it is rarely transferred, with 94% to 97% of fathers not taking at least one day of shared parental leave for the 2014 to 2018 cohorts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The experience of other countries, such as Sweden or Germany, has shown that the introduction of mandatory use-it-or-lose-it "daddy days" significantly increased the take-up rate of paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Portugal has experimented with this model, which increased the take-up rate of shared paternity leave from 596 fathers in 2009 before the reforms, to about 16,400 fathers the year after.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is why the Workers' Party has, in our manifesto, called for a shared parental leave scheme that entitles parents to 24 weeks of Government-paid leave, to be shared between mothers and fathers as they choose, but, crucially, with a minimum of four weeks to be granted to the father and 12 weeks to the mother.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This would replace the existing 16-week maternity and two-week paternity leave entitlements: an increase from 18 weeks to 24 weeks in total of gender-neutral parental leave.

sections.label: Support for single-parent households
sections.summary: The speaker focuses on support for single-parent households and welcomes Action 18 in the White Paper to enhance support for single parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I have spoken about support for parents in the plural and I would now like to switch gears slightly and focus on the topic of support for single-parent households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am heartened to see that one of the action plans, Action 18, introduced in the White Paper seeks to "enhance support for single parents" and I look forward to the concrete initiatives and recommendations to come.

sections.label: Housing concessions for unmarried single parents
sections.summary: Some concessions let unmarried single parents aged 21 and above buy a 3-room flat in a non-mature estate or a resale flat, but they lack equal treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Some concessions have been made, depending on individual case circumstances, such as permitting unmarried single parents aged 21 and above to buy up to a 3-room flat in a non-mature estate from HDB, or a resale flat; but they still do not receive equal treatment to their divorced or widowed counterparts, let alone other families.

sections.label: Unmarried single mothers' income and grants
sections.summary: Median monthly employment income for unmarried single mothers below 35 was $600 in 2017, and the Proximity Housing Grant difference for families and singles is $10,000 to $15,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The median monthly employment income for unmarried single mothers below the age of 35 was $600 in 2017, a number which has hardly changed since 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The $10,000 to $15,000 difference between the Proximity Housing Grant for Families and Singles could amount to a year of mortgage payments or a significant contribution to a child's college fund.

sections.label: Proximity Housing Grant recipients
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee said only five unmarried single-parent families obtained the Proximity Housing Grant for families in the last five years, versus 2,029 divorced or widowed single-parent families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In response to my Parliamentary Question in a previous Sitting on the number of unmarried single parents who have successfully obtained the Proximity Housing Grant for families in the last five years, MND Minister Desmond Lee shared that only five unmarried single-parent families had obtained the grant, in contrast to 2,029 divorced or widowed single-parent families.

sections.label: CPF balances for men and women
sections.summary: Financial literacy and retirement savings issues are not unique to women, but CPF data as of 31 December 2020 show men's balances are 10% higher than women's.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Having adequate financial literacy to support sound financial decision-making throughout one's lifetime and having sufficient savings to support one's retirement are issues not unique to women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, based on CPF data, as of 31 December 2020, we see that CPF members' balances for men are 10% higher than those for women, even though the number of men and women CPF members are roughly equivalent.

sections.label: New approach to women's development
sections.summary: A new approach is needed recognising that policies shape behaviour, and lawmakers must set concrete policy changes to advance women's development in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But critically, what we need is a new approach which recognises that policies shape behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And as lawmakers, we need to set in place concrete policy changes which reflect our collective will to advance women's development in Singapore.

sections.label: Women's Charter 1964
sections.summary: Singapore passed the Women's Charter in 1964 to give women equal rights in marriage and at work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore moved quickly – we passed the Women’s Charter in 1964 and the aim of this legislation was to give women equal rights in marriage and at work.

sections.label: Employment law development actions
sections.summary: Under Area 1, Actions 1 and 2 provide an important development in Singapore's employment law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Under Area 1, Actions 1 and 2 provide an important development in Singapore’s employment law.

sections.label: Guidelines legislated for all employers
sections.summary: If these guidelines are legislated, they will apply more broadly to all employers, even those not employing foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If these guidelines are now legislated, then it will apply more broadly to all employers, even those who do not employ foreign workers.

sections.label: Respite for caregivers
sections.summary: Action 7 provides direct respite for caregivers by adding basic child- and elder-minding services to the Household Services Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Action 7 provides direct respite for caregivers by adding basic child- and elder-minding services to the Household Services Scheme.

sections.label: Fair employment and caregiver support
sections.summary: The Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices will be enshrined in law, and the Household Services Scheme broadened to include child- and elder-minding services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One big development is enshrining the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices into law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This will mean that opportunities will need to be given to people on merit, and irrelevant considerations, such as gender, should not be taken into account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Women are often caregivers in many households, for both the young and the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This paper proposes broadening the Household Services Scheme to include basic child- and elder-minding services, to give families more options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Financial support will be given to caregivers for the elderly with different grants, and access to affordable preschools will be enhanced.

sections.label: Women's employment rate growth
sections.summary: The employment rate for women aged 25 to 64 grew over two decades, rising from 73.2% in 2020 to 75.1% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The employment rate for women aged 25 to 64 has continually grown over the past two decades and, remarkably, continued to increase even during the pandemic from 73.2% in 2020 to 75.1% in 2021 – beating the odds.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements increase
sections.summary: In 2020, close to nine in 10 employees worked in companies providing at least one FWA on a sustained basis, up from more than six in 10 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2020, close to nine in 10 employees worked in companies that provided at least one FWA on a sustained basis, up from more than six in 10 in 2015.

sections.label: White Paper on FWAs
sections.summary: The White Paper sets out plans to strengthen FWAs, with new tripartite guidelines introduced by 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The White Paper has laid out our plans to strengthen and sustain FWAs at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will introduce a new set of tripartite guidelines on FWAs by 2024.

sections.label: Tripartite standard adoption target
sections.summary: MOM and tripartite partners aim to raise company adoption of the voluntary tripartite standard from 27% to 40% of employees by year end.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: As an intermediate milestone, MOM and our tripartite partners aim to increase the adoption of this voluntary tripartite standard on FWAs by companies covering 27% of employees today to 40% at the end of this year.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement for caregivers
sections.summary: Lower-wage caregivers may be eligible for WIS, providing up to $4,000 annually today and up to $4,200 from 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Lower-wage caregivers who are working may also be eligible for the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) Scheme, which provides up to $4,000 in cash and CPF top-ups annually today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: From 2023 onwards, they can receive up to $4,200 in cash and CPF top-ups annually.

sections.label: Enshrining fair employment guidelines
sections.summary: MOM and tripartite partners are enshrining the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices in law to strengthen workplace equal opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We do not tolerate workplace discrimination in any form, certainly not against women, be it for their caregiving responsibilities or their pregnancy status.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: This is why MOM and our tripartite partners are taking a significant step to enshrine the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices in law, strengthening equal opportunities in the workplace.

sections.label: Workplace fairness committee protections
sections.summary: The Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness agreed to look at protecting confidentiality of those reporting discrimination or harassment and protecting them from retaliation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The work of the Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness is ongoing and the committee has agreed to look at protecting the confidentiality of the identity of those who report on discrimination or harassment at the workplace and protecting them against retaliation.

sections.label: Mandarin speech on workplace support
sections.summary: The White Paper sets steps to support Singapore women, including enshrining TGFEP in law, grievance procedures, FWA guidelines around 2024, and 40% tripartite standard adoption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   We have listened to our people and charted out within the White Paper the direction and steps we will take to better support our Singapore women at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will enshrine TGFEP in law to strengthen and uphold principles of fairness at work so that our women will have equal opportunities alongside their male counterparts to pursue and progress in the careers of their choice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Employers will be required to put in place proper grievance handling procedures, protect the confidentiality of those who come forward to report workplace discrimination or harassment and protect them from retaliation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will introduce Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements around 2024 to require employers to fairly and properly consider FWA requests and continue to boost the adoption of the Tripartite Standard to cover 40% of employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We want to provide women and men with the necessary flexibilities at work so that they can pursue their personal or family aspirations while having a good career.

sections.label: Adjusted gender pay gap study
sections.summary: A 2020 MOM and NUS study found an adjusted gender pay gap of 4.3%, showing marked improvement though still improvable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on a study conducted by MOM and NUS in 2020, it was found that there was an adjusted gender pay gap of 4.3%, which has shown a marked improvement, though it can still be improved.

sections.label: Unadjusted gender pay gap
sections.summary: The unadjusted gender pay gap barely changed between 2002 and 2018, with a 16% differential between the two genders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This may have impacted their time and experience at work, leading to delays in career progression and earnings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, there was barely any change in the unadjusted gender pay gap between 2002 and 2018, with a differential of 16% between the two genders.

sections.label: Fathers using paternity leave
sections.summary: According to MSF, only 55% of fathers used up their paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to MSF, only 55% of fathers used up their paternity leave.

sections.label: Paternity leave and family-friendly practices
sections.summary: An NUS 2021 study showed lower-income men, especially in manual labour, were less likely to use paternity leave, prompting suggestions for compulsory leave and rewards for family-friendly employers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a similar vein, an NUS study in 2021 showed that men with lower incomes were less likely to utilise their paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This was especially prominent in those involved in manual labour.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, could I suggest for provisions to be made to allow for some amount of paternity leave to be made compulsory?

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, employers or institutions which are able to adopt such family-friendly practices should be rewarded for their commitment to gender equality in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These efforts are not easy to adopt, especially since it also relies on the mindset change and support of society to make it work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is also in line with the Government's moves to encourage marriage and parenthood to boost the total fertility rate.

sections.label: Sharing household responsibilities
sections.summary: Fathers, parents, educators, employers, colleagues and consumers are urged to share household responsibilities and set good examples.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As fathers, when we make an effort to share the mental load and burden of household responsibilities; as parents and educators when we decide what kind of examples we set with our behaviour; as employers and colleagues when we show understanding to fellow parents at work or as consumers where we take a stand to not consume sexist content.

sections.label: Welcoming White Paper action plans
sections.summary: The speaker says it should be their choice, not an imposed judgement, and welcomes the 25 concrete action plans in the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Let it be their choice and not a decision or judgement that we impose on them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome the 25 concrete action plans that have been tabled in the White Paper.

sections.label: Employers consider flexible work requests
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes MOM news that employers must consider staff requests for flexible work arrangements by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In that regard, I welcome the recent news by MOM that employers must consider staff requests for FWAs by 2024.

sections.label: KidSTART expansion welcomed
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes KidSTART's expansion and hopes its content and delivery are not diluted as it grows.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In that regard, I welcome the expansion of KidSTART and hope that, as the programme continues to expand, the content and delivery are not diluted.

sections.label: Women on MENDAKI board
sections.summary: Despite a female CEO, only seven of MENDAKI's 21 board members are women.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For example, even though MENDAKI has a female Chief Executive Officer, only seven out of 21 members on its Board of Directors are women.

sections.label: White Paper on Women's Development
sections.summary: The White Paper signals the Government's direction towards a fairer, inclusive society where men and women are equals, requiring all of society to play its part.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With this, mothers can feel reassured enough to return to work and the children will also receive support in terms of their education and mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, the White Paper on Women's Development is a strong signal of the Government's direction towards a fairer and more inclusive society where men and women are seen as equals and complementary in building a better Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: While the Government leads the way in legislating these proposals, society, as a whole, must play its part.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is all hands on deck, regardless of gender or age, whether you are a student or a worker, employer or employee, private or public sector.

sections.label: Equal parental leave shares urged
sections.summary: The speaker urges equal default sharing of parental leave, with flexibility to reallocate by mutual agreement and a minimum period per parent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, maternity leave is 16 weeks, paternity leave, two weeks, and fathers can share up to four weeks of their wives’ maternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is inconsistent with our move to change mindsets on gender roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to change it to equal shares by default, with flexibility to reallocate parental leave between the couple based on mutual agreement, subject to a minimum period for each parent.

sections.label: CPF top-up tax relief cap
sections.summary: The Government is raising the CPF top-up tax relief cap from $7,000 to $8,000 to improve caregivers' retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Another measure that the Government is changing to improve the retirement adequacy of caregivers is to raise the CPF top-up tax relief cap from $7,000 to $8,000.

sections.label: 30% target commitment question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will commit to setting a target of 30% within three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Government commit to setting a target of 30% within three years?

sections.label: 2010 caregiver statistics
sections.summary: In 2010, about 8% of residents aged 18 to 69 provided regular care, with 37% of caregivers reporting almost a decade of care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2010, approximately 8% of residents aged between 18 and 69 years provided regular care to a friend or family member, with 37% of caregivers reporting that they had been providing care for almost a decade.

sections.label: Caregiving as leaving-work reason
sections.summary: About 6% of residents cited caregiving as the main reason for leaving or not seeking jobs, and 15% of women cited family responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to a 2019 answer by the Minister for Health to a Parliamentary Question by then-NMP Anthea Ong, about 6% of Singapore residents – male and female – cited caregiving to family members as the main reason for leaving their jobs or not looking for one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In a reply by Minister of State Gan Siow Huang to Parliamentary Questions by Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Ms Joan Pereira earlier this year, 15% of women aged 25 to 64 cited family-related responsibilities as their main reason for being outside the labour force in 2020, while 6% worked part-time due to family or personal commitments.

sections.label: Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs
sections.summary: The White Paper states the Government will introduce Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs by 2024 requiring employers to consider FWA requests fairly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The White Paper states that the Government will introduce a new set of Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs by 2024, which will require employers to "consider FWA requests from employees fairly and properly".

sections.label: Six days family care leave
sections.summary: All Singaporean employees should get up to six days of leave for young children or immediate family members with long-term illnesses or disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a start, all Singaporean employees should be granted up to six days of leave to look after their young children or immediate family members with long-term illnesses or disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first three days should be paid by the employer, with the remaining days paid by the Government.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant increase
sections.summary: The White Paper stated the Home Caregiving Grant quantum will increase next year from $200 to up to $400 monthly for low-income HDB households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The White Paper stated that the Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) quantum will be increased next year from $200 to up to $400 per month for low-income households living in HDB flats.

sections.label: Dementia sufferers claiming HCG
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Minister can clarify if dementia sufferers can claim for HCG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
