sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify if dementia sufferers can claim for HCG?

sections.label: Respite care places December 2021
sections.summary: The Minister for Health said that as at end December 2021 there were over 450 respite care places.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As at end December 2021, there were over 450 respite care places, according to the Minister for Health in response to a Parliamentary Question by Ms Nadia Samdin.

sections.label: Nursing home expansion plans
sections.summary: A Member asks MOF, MOH and MSF to elaborate on plans to expand nursing homes and adult disability homes up to 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am not suggesting that everyone rush to put their parents in nursing homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the reality is that with longer lifespans, fewer children and more Singaporeans working overseas, we can expect an increasing demand for long-term residential care for elders and the disabled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As of end-2020, 90% of the 16,300 nursing home beds were utilised, up from 85% in June 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can MOF, MOH and MSF elaborate on their plans to expand nursing homes and adult disability homes up to 2030?

sections.label: White Paper on women equality
sections.summary: The White Paper is described as an important marker on the road to equality for women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The White Paper is an important marker on this road to equality for women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We have not arrived, but we know the road to travel and the final destination.

sections.label: Internalising respect for women
sections.summary: Respect and equality for women require internalisation by the majority as basic values, aiming for deep mindset change.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But beyond that, in a more fundamental way, when we talk about respect for women, equality of women, it requires an internalisation by the majority that these are basic values; that these are values which we cherish, which we hold dear.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And I have said, when we started the Conversations in September 2020, that our aim is to work towards a deep mindset change, to build a society where every boy and girl grows up imbibing the value of gender equality.

sections.label: Conversations and White Paper impact
sections.summary: The Conversations from September 2020 and the White Paper are said to have had a significant psychological impact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: From September 2020, the Conversations, this White Paper, I believe, have had a significant psychological impact and moved us further along the path.

sections.label: Sexual offences outside Parliament
sections.summary: The passage states that sexual offences outside Parliament can lead to jail and caning, and that a male MP could face jail and caning for egregious conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He touched a woman over her skirt during an MRT ride.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He was sentenced to 18 days in jail.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Nothing as graphic as what you see happened in the Australian parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He was sentenced to nine months' jail and three strokes of the cane.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If you do these things outside Parliament, you are likely to get jailed and caned.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think it is quite unthinkable that something like this can or will happen in a parliamentary context in Singapore but, if it did, a male Member of Parliament is likely to go to jail and be caned for some of the more egregious conduct.

sections.label: Advice to wives
sections.summary: The advice included that wives should mimic Doraemon's voice, giggle coyly, avoid home clothes, put on make-up, use humorous words and avoid nagging.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The advice included the following: that the wives should mimic the voice of a Japanese cartoon character, Doraemon, when speaking to their husbands; wives should giggle coyly; wives should avoid wearing home clothes and put on make-up; wives should use humorous words and avoid nagging.

sections.label: Police response to beating wives
sections.summary: In Singapore, if you beat your wives or vice versa, the Police will come looking for you.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In Singapore, let me tell you, if you beat your wives or vice versa, the Police will come looking for you.

sections.label: Women's safety survey results
sections.summary: The 2018 public perception survey showed 93% of women feel safe in Singapore, and Gallup's 2020 survey showed 97% feel safe walking alone at night.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The 2018 public perception survey showed that 93% of our women feel safe in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2020, Gallup's Law and Order survey, 97% of Singapore residents – obviously men and women – feel safe walking alone on the streets at night.

sections.label: Family violence task force
sections.summary: MHA and MSF set up a task force on family violence in February 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: MHA and MSF set up a task force on family violence in February 2020.

sections.label: Protection orders and review
sections.summary: The passage states specific persons such as the Director-General of Social Welfare will be empowered to apply for Personal Protection Orders, and the White Paper will be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You really do not want every such situation to end up in the matrimonial Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will also empower specific persons, such as the Director-General of Social Welfare, to apply for Personal Protection Orders on behalf of those at risk in certain situations – like that mother who was clearly being abused but did not want to report her son.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This will be very resource-intensive and, therefore, will take time to implement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In that context, I have shown you some examples – or I call them vignettes and illustrations – of how things happen in some other countries, some things that had happened, and what it reflects and how the road we have taken has made pretty much some of these things quite unthinkable in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will need to look again at this White Paper and the recommendations, continually review, see how far we have come.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And I hope that we can all work to make Singapore a place where every girl and woman can achieve her fullest potential.

sections.label: Caregiver Support Action Plan launch
sections.summary: In 2019, MOH launched the Caregiver Support Action Plan to support caregiving for seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In 2019, MOH launched the Caregiver Support Action Plan to support caregiving for seniors.

sections.label: Household Services Scheme expansion
sections.summary: MOM recently announced plans to broaden the Household Services Scheme to provide basic elder-minding and child-minding services.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: MOM recently announced plans to broaden the Household Services Scheme to provide basic elder-minding and child-minding services.

sections.label: Nursing homes for highest needs
sections.summary: Nursing homes should be reserved for those with the highest care needs and no family support.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Some may turn to nursing homes to provide care.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: However, nursing homes should be reserved for those with the highest care needs and no family support.

sections.label: MOH exploring future care support
sections.summary: MOH is exploring further future support to enhance the care ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: MOH is, therefore, exploring further future support to enhance the care ecosystem.

sections.label: Grant increase for lower-income families
sections.summary: The grant will be increased from $200 per month to up to $400 per month, with more help for lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The grant will be increased from $200 per month to up to $400 per month, with more help provided to lower-income families.

sections.label: Community care service subsidies
sections.summary: A care recipient using these community care services may benefit from subsidies of more than $8,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: A care recipient using these community care services may benefit from subsidies of more than $8,000 per year.

sections.label: Women in mosque boards and Syariah Court
sections.summary: 122 women serve on Mosque Management Boards, and women make up 66% of Syariah Court leadership, led by its first woman Senior President.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To answer Dr Wan Rizal's question, there are, currently, 122 women who have become members of the various Mosque Management Boards.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Syariah Court is led by the first woman Senior President, and she is supported by other women legal professionals, such as the President, Registrar as well as Assistant Registrar, with women making up 66% of the Syariah Court leadership.

sections.label: Online safety codes and research
sections.summary: A 2022 Sunlight AfA study found 43% of respondents favoured stricter enforcement, and MCI announced Codes of Practice on online safety.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: A baseline study commissioned by Sunlight AfA in January 2022 found that 43% of respondents considered stricter enforcement of relevant laws to be the most effective solution to reduce gender-based online harms.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In line with global trends and citizens' desire for stronger safeguards in the digital space, MCI recently announced the introduction of Codes of Practice to raise the baseline standard for online safety so as to minimise exposure to harmful content; empower users to report and prevent the further spread of harmful content; and ensure online platforms remain accountable on their measures and processes to keep users safe.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Moving forward, Sunlight AfA will also be developing a research roadmap to inform future research priorities and measures to address online harms.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As MCI develops these Codes of Practice, we will consult community stakeholders, including AfA members, to ensure efforts to nurture a safe online environment are tailored to meet the needs of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Equal duties and choices for women
sections.summary: The speaker calls for empowering all Singaporeans and says duties to women and choices open to women must equal those for men.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Let us walk together on this journey and empower all Singaporeans – men and women alike – to pursue their aspirations freely and to the fullest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I will not just speak as a Member of the House or a Member of the front bench, but also as a son, a father and a husband.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: At the core of this debate are the relationships that all of us have with women in our lives, at our workplaces, in our country.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And our duty to women should be equal to our duties to all fellow citizens and the choices open to women must be equal to those open to men.

sections.label: Young father's assumption on bias
sections.summary: As a young father, the speaker thought discrimination and biases against women would eventually be scrubbed out by modern society's norms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: You see, as a young father, I had thought that whatever discrimination and biases there were against women, it will be alright, my children will be alright, our daughters will be alright because these would, eventually, be scrubbed out by the norms of a modern society.

sections.label: Understanding bias through daughters
sections.summary: The speaker says children are born without bias, but through his daughters' formative years he better understood social expectations and prejudices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: All children, sons and daughters, are born into this world with no bias against men or women, like my own daughters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But through my daughters' eyes, during their formative years, I better understood the lived experience of social expectations and prejudices.

sections.label: Policies to accelerate a new future
sections.summary: Enacting policies such as universal education, the Women's Charter and White Paper recommendations can catalyse and accelerate a new future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: By enacting policies, such as universal access to education, the Women’s Charter and all the various recommendations in the White Paper before the House today, we can catalyse and help accelerate into that new future.

sections.label: Childcare, infant care, paternity leave
sections.summary: The passage states childcare leave was introduced in 2004, infant care leave in 2008, one week of paternity leave in 2013 and a second week in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In 2004, we introduced childcare leave, and then, infant care leave in 2008 as we saw men performing more of such roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Then, in 2013, I believe, we introduced one week of paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And as we saw more men participating, we introduced a second week in 2017.

sections.label: White Paper recommendations and initiatives
sections.summary: The White Paper recommendations balance equality with differences between women and men, listing anti-discriminatory measures, FWAs, caregiver support, elective egg freezing, stiffer sexual offence penalties and family support infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The recommendations in the White Paper are careful in recognising and striking this balance – championing equality, especially of opportunities and progression, but yet recognising the beautiful differences between women and men.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: There are many practical initiatives – anti-discriminatory measures in the workplace, FWAs, stronger support for caregivers, allowing elective egg freezing, and upholding stiffer penalties for sexual offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Of particular importance are the moves to strengthen the family support infrastructure, which are empowering for women at various stages of their lives.

sections.label: Expanding recipients needs more budget
sections.summary: Expanding or doubling the number of recipients requires more budget, which must come from taxes, and if taxes cannot be raised, the money's source is questioned.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And if you want to expand it, double it, expand the number of recipients, you are looking at more budget.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It has to come from some taxes and if you cannot raise taxes, if you object to raising taxes, then where will the money come from?

sections.label: Speaker's support for the White Paper
sections.summary: The speaker describes a collective duty to support women, dispel unconscious bias, uphold meritocracy and help caregivers, calling equality to freedom of choice the heart of the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As a son, father and husband, and a Member of this House, I see our collective duty to support women in whatever they set out to do and accelerate away from our antiquated past of women and men stereotypes, at home, at work, in society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The future that we envision must be a society that dispels unconscious bias, promotes the right value of mutual respect between all individuals, upholds meritocracy and provides as much support as we can to enable caregivers to find better balance in their roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In my mind, this equality to freedom of choice is the heart of this White Paper and the reason why I strongly support it.

sections.label: Working from home and women's careers
sections.summary: The article identified that prolonged working from home may dampen women's career development, cutting female executives off from informal company channels and making resources harder to obtain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Among the issues highlighted in the article, it was identified that a prolonged period of working from home may, in fact, have a dampening effect on the career development of women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of the effects was the result in female executives being cut off from informal channels within the company and then, subsequently, encountering difficulties in obtaining resources necessary for work through informal company and industry networks.

sections.label: Assisting return-to-work mothers
sections.summary: Return-to-work moms may face skills gaps, lost business networks and limited knowledge of openings, so NTUC's e2i or Women and Family initiative could conduct career coaching and provide skills upgrading courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many of these return-to-work moms will, inevitably, experience a skills-gap issue where their knowledge about their trade could have become obsolete over time, they could have also lost business networks that they used to have, and they might not be fully up-to-date on the type of professional openings that are available on the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To better assist return-to-work moms, it would be good if NTUC’s e2i division or their Women and Family initiative can conduct unique career coaching sessions to ensure that women returning to work are fully aware of the type of opportunities available in the market and they also have access to skills upgrading courses that enable these return-to-work moms to pick up new and relevant skills that will make them a better fit for the market.

sections.label: Support for mumpreneurs and working women
sections.summary: The passage calls for more mumpreneur networks, possible start-up grants and micro-financing, and whole-of-society and company efforts to support women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Indeed, having more of these networks, like "Mumpreneurs-Go-Places", for example, could help to coalesce and bond this group of mumpreneurs, who would then be able to provide mutual advice, help, support and guidance for one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It would be good if the Government could also perhaps consider providing some start-up grants and support for such mumpreneurs or perhaps explore avenues of micro-financing that would be useful to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Because, while the Government can take the lead in outlining concrete steps to support women, it takes a whole-of-society effort to actually move this needle significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Solving issues, such as unconscious biases and glass ceilings at work, require companies to take proactive steps, such as sponsoring the careers of high potential female executives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Resolving the challenges faced by working moms and return-to-work moms requires not only strong support from their family members, but also a system to integrate and reintegrate these women into the professional working network.

sections.label: Women's housework and caregiving
sections.summary: A Government survey found women in dual income households were five times more likely than men to manage housework and caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: A recent Government survey, for example, found that women in dual income households were five times more likely than men to be managing housework and giving care.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant increase
sections.summary: The increase in the Home Caregiving Grant is welcomed as a significant increase in support for low-income households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Notably, the increase in Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) is welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It is a significant increase in support for low-income households.

sections.label: Respite care funding and stress
sections.summary: Funds may allow caregivers to get needed respite care when stress becomes overpowering, and the passage highlights enhancing respite care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It may also mean having funds to get the much-needed respite care, when the stress on the caregiver becomes overpowering and she needs a break.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I wish to highlight the importance of enhancing respite care.

sections.label: MOH respite care review suggestions
sections.summary: The passage hopes MOH will consider increasing institutional respite care capacity and exploring flexible financing, including extended family members' MediSave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As MOH reviews the respite care landscape, I hope that MOH will also consider: (a) increasing institutional capacity for respite care across Singapore, even as MOH explores home-based respite care, because not all homes are suitable and caregivers, usually, prefer to keep their loved ones near as they may have separation anxiety; (b) exploring more flexible financing options, including greater use of extended family members' MediSave, to pay for respite care services, beyond enhancing HCG, which works like a subsidy.

sections.label: MDWs and caregiving households
sections.summary: The passage urges the Government to be more sensitive to households needing MDWs for caregiving, especially middle- and lower-income ones.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: While I understand that MDWs, by virtue of them being in a foreign country, are assumed to be of lesser resource and that over-reliance on MDWs is more a bane than a boon, the reality is that families and, therefore, women of such households need MDWs to support caregiving at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge the Government to pay greater attention to this matter and be more sensitive to the circumstances and needs of such households, especially those of middle- and lower-income, because time taken to settle these disputes means time away from productive and fulfilling work.

sections.label: Support for White Paper Area 3
sections.summary: The speaker supports Area 3 actions in the White Paper and highlights protecting girls from violence or sexual misdemeanours at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, I believe the actions set out in Area 3 of the White Paper are pertinent and I support them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But I also wish to highlight the importance of protecting girls from violent or sexual misdemeanours at home.

sections.label: Significance of White Paper
sections.summary: The speaker believes the White Paper is significant and valuable for setting out specific actions to support Singapore women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my questions raised, Sir, I believe the White Paper holds great significance in our continued journey to support Singapore women to fulfil their fullest potential and aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: So much has been said in this House, the White Paper's greatest value is that it sets out specific actions to be taken.

sections.label: Grant for paid caregiver leave
sections.summary: The Government should consider providing a grant for employers to offer paid leave to caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Government should consider providing a grant for employers to offer paid leave to caregivers.

sections.label: Tax breaks for caregivers
sections.summary: The Government should consider tax breaks for caregivers financing unsubsidised items like diapers and nutritional supplements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, I hope the Government can consider providing tax breaks for caregivers who have to finance items that are not subsidised under the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF) such as diapers and nutritional supplements.

sections.label: Equipping AIC for caregivers
sections.summary: The Agency for Integrated Care must be adequately equipped as a one-stop centre to support all kinds of caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) as a one-stop centre for caregivers must be adequately equipped as a one-stop centre for caregivers, must be adequately equipped to provide support for all kinds of caregivers.

sections.label: Caregiver's Day or Week
sections.summary: A Caregiver's Day or Caregiver's Week should be considered to create awareness and recognition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, we should consider having a Caregiver’s Day or even a Caregiver’s Week to create awareness and recognition.

sections.label: Women's labour force participation rise
sections.summary: A Singapore labour force participation survey for 2012 to 2021 shows women's participation rising from 57.7% to 64.2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we all know, in a recently released labour force participation survey in Singapore for the years from 2012 to 2021, it is very heartening to note and observe an increase in women's participation, from 57.7% to 64.2%.

sections.label: Maternity leave duration concerns
sections.summary: People hope maternity leave increases from four to six months but worry about negative repercussions for those away on leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While they hope and wish for an increase in the duration of maternity leave from the current four months to six months, deep inside, they are also worried about the negative repercussions for those who have to be away in view of their maternity leave.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements guidelines
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements and boosting adoption of Tripartite Standards on Flexible Work Arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In short, we can go on and on and on advocating, but what is the outcome since then and now?" Sir, I can only comfort the leader but, deep in my heart, I know what she said is the real truth and the improvements could have been more and better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I certainly welcome the move to introduce the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements and boost its adoption of Tripartite Standards on Flexible Work Arrangements.

sections.label: Protection from sexual and family violence
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes increased punishment for sexual offences to enhance protection and support for victims of family violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More efforts are needed to protect women from such violence committed by men, and the worst ones involves victims of any sexual harassment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I certainly welcome the move to increase the punishment for these sexual offences aimed at enhancing protection and support for victims or survivors of any family violence.

sections.label: Child-minding and maintenance payments
sections.summary: The speaker asks about child-minding centres and urges ex-husbands to pay maintenance timely for their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is there a centre that can provide child-minding services so that the affected parents can feel reassured while they are at work?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge the ex-husbands to show more concern towards your former life partners for their sacrifices in raising your children, by ensuring that the payment of maintenance is done in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Please do not make them wait or, worse, plead for the money needed to raise your children, who are born out of the love you once shared with your former partner.

sections.label: Respecting and protecting women
sections.summary: The speaker cites a hadith on righteous wives and says every man must respect and protect every woman with love and care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Please remember that no amount of money comes close to a wife’s sacrifice when she bears our children, and cares for and nurtures them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In closing, I remind myself and all husbands of a hadith, or saying, of the Prophet: “The world is but an adornment, and the best adornment to the world are the pious and righteous wives.” (In English): Sir, each and every man must learn to respect and protect every woman with love and care as though they are part of your family members.

sections.label: White paper on Singapore women
sections.summary: The paper reflects Singaporeans' voices and its 25 Action Plans aim to improve women's lives and advance society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The paper reflects the manifold voices and collective aspirations of Singaporeans, both women and men alike.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We hope the paper’s 25 Action Plans will not only improve the lives of Singapore women, but, as a whole, advance our society.

sections.label: Three areas of action
sections.summary: The three areas are uplifting caregivers, protecting women in sports, and developing national standards reflecting women's needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: First, we will uplift caregivers, many of whom are women, by working closely with the community to lighten their load; second, we will ensure the protection of women in sports; and third, we will develop national standards for products, services and procedures to better reflect the needs of women.

sections.label: Caregiver support networks for mental health
sections.summary: PA, NCSS and SG Cares Volunteer Centres will work with Caregiver Alliance Limited to link caregivers of persons with mental health conditions into mutual support networks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: From next month onwards, PA, NCSS and SG Cares Volunteer Centres will work with Caregiver Alliance Limited to link caregivers of persons with mental health conditions together to form networks of mutual support.

sections.label: Buddy programme for disability caregivers
sections.summary: Through the Alliance for Action on Caregivers of Persons with Disabilities, NCSS and SG Enable will create a buddy programme pairing experienced caregivers with new ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Through the Alliance for Action (AfA) on Caregivers of Persons with Disabilities, NCSS and SG Enable will collaborate with community partners to create a buddy programme that pairs experienced caregivers with new ones.

sections.label: Safe Sport Unified Code
sections.summary: The Safe Sport Commission developed a Safe Sport Unified Code that sets out a common understanding of misconduct, abuse and harassment in sport.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Since then, the Safe Sport Commission has, over a nine-month consultative process, developed a Safe Sport Unified Code to enhance the protection of women in sports.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: First, the Code has set out a common reference point and understanding of what constitutes misconduct, abuse and harassment in sport.

sections.label: Disciplinary Panel for misconduct
sections.summary: A Disciplinary Panel will be established to hear and review allegations of misconduct under the Unified Code.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Third, we will be establishing a Disciplinary Panel to hear and review allegations of misconduct under the Unified Code.

sections.label: New gender strategy developed
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore and the Singapore Standards Council recently developed a new gender strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To this end, Enterprise Singapore (ESG) and the Singapore Standards Council have recently developed a new gender strategy.

sections.label: Employment of Singapore women
sections.summary: Three-quarters of Singapore women between 25 and 64 years old are employed at the workplace today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the workplace today, three-quarters of Singapore women between 25 and 64 years old are employed.

sections.label: Female boardroom representation
sections.summary: Female representation stands at just 17.6% in Singapore's top 100 primary listed companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the boardroom, female representation stands at just 17.6% in our top 100 primary listed companies.

sections.label: Women in STEM work
sections.summary: Women account for only a third of employed residents working in STEM.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Yet, women account for only a third of employed residents working in STEM.

sections.label: Caregiver income and retirement
sections.summary: Caregiver's income decreases by 63% on average, reducing their ability to save for retirement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Emotional labour aside, caregiver's income decreases by 63% on average, reducing their ability to save for retirement.

sections.label: Elective egg freezing steps
sections.summary: The speaker appreciates steps on elective egg freezing, giving women time and space to make choices instead of rushing into starting a family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On this note, I appreciate the steps we are taking on elective egg freezing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With this, women can have the time and space to make choices instead of rushing headlong into starting a family.

sections.label: Work and family finances
sections.summary: For some families, working may reduce ComCare or raise HDB rental fees, leaving them financially worse off than staying at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For some families, work may, inevitably, reduce ComCare or increased HDB rental fees, such that they are in a financially worse position than should she stay at home.

sections.label: Support for offenders' families
sections.summary: Many male offenders leave behind women who need proactive support from incarceration to release and reintegration, not chance visits or referrals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For many male offenders in prison, they leave behind wives, sisters, mothers, daughters outside to wait and face the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We must reach out more proactively to these women and their families to provide support from the point of incarceration to release and reintegration and not leave this assistance to chanced house visits by our teams on the ground or relying on referral pathways in the male offenders' hands.

sections.label: Negative stereotypes against Malay women
sections.summary: The study hoped for more efforts to overcome negative stereotypes that could complicate Malay women's efforts to climb the ladder of success.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The study also hoped that more efforts can be implemented to overcome negative stereotypes that could further complicate the efforts of our Malay women in climbing the ladder of success.

sections.label: White Paper policies and opportunities
sections.summary: The White Paper's policies do not grant women opportunities and rights at the expense of men but seek to improve a society where all contributions are recognised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The policies in this White Paper do not grant women opportunities and rights at the expense of men.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They seek to improve on our current system – a society in which all contributions are recognised and respected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In my own generation, I see how equitable access to opportunities have catapulted women into lives that our mothers and grandmothers could only dream of.

sections.label: White Paper support action plans
sections.summary: The White Paper captured the Government's action plans to enhance support in equal workplace opportunities and recognition and support for caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Having been part of the consultation process, I am glad that the White Paper has captured the Government's action plans to enhance support, especially in two areas: one, equal opportunities at the workplace; and two, recognition and support for caregivers.

sections.label: Mentoring platform for women
sections.summary: Agencies like Workforce Singapore and NTUC should provide a common platform or one-stop portal for job-matching, transition training and mentors for women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To facilitate more of these mentoring efforts, I would like to suggest for agencies, such as Workforce Singapore and NTUC, to provide a common platform or a one-stop portal that offers resources and information on job-matching opportunities, transition training programmes as well as an available pool of mentors that women at work or re-entering the workforce can connect to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This will be especially helpful for women who have been stay-home caregivers for many years and require support transitioning back to the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad to share that, in partnership with fellow hon Member Yeo Wan Ling and NTUC Women and Family Unit, my constituency in Jalan Kayu will be implementing a women-mentoring-women programme to support such efforts.

sections.label: MediSave Care withdrawal limits
sections.summary: The MediSave Care Scheme lets individuals with severe disabilities or their spouses withdraw up to $200 monthly, capped at $2,400 yearly, for long-term care needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Additionally, I understand that the current MediSave Care Scheme allows individuals with severe disabilities or their spouses to withdraw up to $200 monthly, with the cap of $2,400 per year to supplement long-term care needs.

sections.label: Mindset shifts for women's progress
sections.summary: Mindset shifts are the foundational factor for women's progress in Singapore, and empowering women is not a zero-sum game but benefits society as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development have rightly identified, mindset shifts in our society remain the foundational factor undergirding the progress of women in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While it is difficult to see the effectiveness of mindset shifts in the short term, it is the most needed to materialise in all the areas that we are pursuing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that the mindset shift towards empowering women need not be seen as a zero-sum game where the rights of one gender have to be compromised over the other and men are supposed to give something up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Rather, it is the empowerment of women to progress in society as a whole where they reach their fullest potential to become active contributors to realising a fairer and more inclusive society for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thus, in order to fully appreciate the progress of women in Singapore, in our society, we need to also consider the immense support and understanding that our fathers, brothers, husbands and sons have been giving to us in this enduring partnership in women's development.

sections.label: Singapore adjusted gender pay gap
sections.summary: Singapore's adjusted gender pay gap decreased from 8.8% in 2002 to 4.3% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For example, the discrepancy in Singapore's adjusted gender pay gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This has decreased from 8.8% in 2002 to 4.3% in 2020.

sections.label: Survey on workplace gender discrimination
sections.summary: A survey by NTUC and PAP Women's Wing found 23% of respondents believe there is gender discrimination in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: According to a survey by NTUC and PAP Women's Wing, 23% of respondents believe there is gender discrimination in the workplace.

sections.label: Women in NTUC Enterprise leadership
sections.summary: In the NTUC Enterprise group, about half the leadership team are women and female board representation is about 34%, exceeding Singapore Institute of Directors guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Within the NTUC Enterprise group that I work at, I am proud that, in our leadership team, about half of them are women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The female representation on our board of directors is about 34%, already exceeding the targeted minimum guidelines that the Singapore Institute of Directors is advocating for all boards.

sections.label: Frequency of mansplaining
sections.summary: Mansplaining is so common that it has a name, but this has not made it less frequent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How is this okay? "Mansplaining" – in fact, Minister Ong Ye Kung also referred to it – is so common that there is a name for it, but this has not made it less frequent.

sections.label: Women's equal place in society
sections.summary: A male editor wrote that many women prefer generous husbands over partners who expect equal sharing of household expenses, which the speaker calls astonishing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In a recent article in the newspaper – in fact, just slightly more than a week ago – a male editor wrote, "Frankly, many women prefer generous husbands and would think poorly of partners who expect them to share household expenses equally like how some couples split dining bills when they are dating." This is truly astonishing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: But we should pause and think if such asymmetry is something that we should be proud of.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We become a better society when women are more equal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: That women should have an equal place in society is right in itself.

sections.label: Caregivers' hours and employment
sections.summary: Duke NUS and MSF surveys show caregivers spend 36 to 38 hours weekly on caregiving, and almost half do not hold a job.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Duke NUS and MSF surveys illustrate that caregivers spend an average of 36 to 38 hours a week on caregiving, depending on the level of needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Almost half of the caregivers surveyed do not hold a job and of those who do, 26% of them had their work affected by caregiving.

sections.label: Women and CPF retirement sums
sections.summary: 2018 MOM statistics showed women greatly outnumbered men in not hitting the CPF Basic Retirement Sum at age 55, with longer life expectancy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The 2018 MOM statistics also showed that women greatly outnumbered men in not being able to hit the CPF Basic Retirement Sum at age 55 and, at the same time, have a longer life expectancy.

sections.label: Caregiving allowance and CPF support
sections.summary: The speaker urges a calibrated monthly caregiving allowance with CPF contributions for caregivers who reduced or stopped work, covering out-of-pocket care expenses.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am encouraged to hear that the Home Care Giving (HCG) grant will be further enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I believe we can still take a greater stride to support caregivers, given their significant loss of income, by providing a calibrated monthly caregiving allowance with CPF contributions for those who have reduced work, or stopped work to be caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Caregiving involves many out-of-pocket expenses, from medical supplements to transportation for medical appointments, to medical and mobility aids.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: These costs are even more significant for those who are disqualified from subsidies due to the AV of the care recipients' property.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Caregiving allowance is not meant to be an income replacement, but an allowance to support these out-of-pocket care expenses in caregiving and also basic personal subsistence, without disincentivising work.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Various OECD countries have formulated ways in which caregivers can be compensated, whether via allowances or care recipient benefits, which we can study to formulate one suitable and sustainable for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The dedication of our singles to care for our seniors should be recognised and advanced in tangible ways, with policies that facilitate building a retirement safety net for them.

sections.label: Employers giving preferred shifts
sections.summary: Managers give employees their preferred shift for care duties, and 126 companies adopted this model since DOT began enrolling employer partners in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What it means is that managers give employees their preferred shift to accommodate their care duties at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And since DOT started enrolling employer partners in 2018, 126 companies have adopted this model successfully, where single mothers have managed to plan their daily routines more efficiently, reducing work-care conflicts, when they do not have to juggle multiple different shifts within the same week.

sections.label: Single mothers turning down promotions
sections.summary: Single mothers in rental flats that DOT works with turn down promotions to stay within the salary band for the existing rental rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: After securing a job and income, many want to clear their arrears or other debts that they may be owing to friends and family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is not uncommon for single mothers living in rental flats that Daughter Of Tomorrow (DOT) works with to turn down promotions from their employers so that they will stay within the salary band for the existing rental rate.

sections.label: Rent grace period public flats
sections.summary: An automatic 12-month grace period before adjusting rent in public rental flats, post-employment, will help these families greatly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: An automatic 12-month grace period before adjusting rent in public rental flats, post-employment, will help these families greatly.

sections.label: AWARE SHE Project communal housing
sections.summary: At DOT, the speaker collaborated with AWARE's SHE Project, which provides two years of communal housing for low-income single mothers and their children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While at DOT, I collaborated with AWARE's SHE Project, which provides two years of communal housing for two to three low-income single mothers and their children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They offered peer support to each other and pooled resources for domestic and childcare needs, which helped them retain their jobs and build up their financial resources.

sections.label: Subsidies for SME harassment training
sections.summary: The speaker recommends Government subsidies for training or diversity and inclusion coaches to support SMEs facing harassment and discrimination issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Larger companies and MNCs often have sufficient resources and services to help them address harassment and discrimination, but many SMEs might not, and they have very real operational challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I recommend that the Government provide subsidies for training on such matters, or for “diversity and inclusion” coaches to support SMEs in their culture transition.

sections.label: Expanding National Service to care vocations
sections.summary: One way is to expand the scope of National Service to include care vocations, enlisting both young men and women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One way is to expand the scope of National Service to include care vocations, enlisting both young men and women.

sections.label: Care vocations in National Service
sections.summary: Including care vocations in National Service will reduce stress and make care work a shared civic responsibility in an un-gendered manner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Including care vocations in National Service (NS) to support the community with their caregiving needs will help reduce the stress of our people and our workforce and, more critically, for care work to be seen as a shared civic responsibility in a nation with a rapidly ageing population, in an un-gendered manner.

sections.label: De-conflicting work and care
sections.summary: De-conflicting work and care is the urgent priority to advance women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: De-conflicting work and care is the urgent priority to advance women.

sections.label: National Anti-Violence Helpline enhancement
sections.summary: The Government will enhance the National Anti-Violence Helpline to include a text messaging service or app for discrete queries or reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government also, in response to my previous Parliamentary Question, will enhance the National Anti-Violence Helpline to include a text messaging service or app, which would allow discrete queries or reporting.

sections.label: Rehabilitation of family violence perpetrators
sections.summary: The Taskforce on Family Violence recommended strengthening perpetrator rehabilitation, including mandatory counselling programmes and treatment, to reduce recurring violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, beyond survivors, we also need to assist men to get the help that they need, be it in parenting, anger management or conflict de-escalation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I am heartened that the Taskforce on Family Violence has recommended to strengthen the rehabilitation of perpetrators, including mandatory counselling programmes (MCP) and treatment, to reduce the risk of violence recurring.

sections.label: Casa Raudha beneficiaries housing and employment
sections.summary: Casa Raudha data shows beneficiaries moving to rental housing rose from 40% in 2017 to over 70% in 2021, with almost two-thirds unemployed upon discharge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Based on data from Casa Raudha, the number of beneficiaries who went on to live in rental housing upon discharge has gone up from 40% in 2017 to over 70% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Further, almost two-thirds of them are still unemployed upon discharge despite training and upskilling efforts.

sections.label: Netherlands Orange House crisis shelter
sections.summary: The Orange House, established in 2011 in the Netherlands, provides shelter and care in a safe but open and visible city-centre setting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the Netherlands, The Orange House, established in 2011, changed this thinking behind crisis shelters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Orange House, located right in the city centre, provides shelter and care in a safe but open and visible setting within the community.

sections.label: Visible shelter and whole-of-nation approach
sections.summary: A similar visible, accessible shelter could empower survivors and signal society's support, with the White Paper and Taskforce recommendations moving towards intervention, cooperation and rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Perhaps, we can consider a similar, more visible and accessible shelter which will not only be empowering to survivors but also send a strong signal to the rest of society that we stand by them, alongside them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With greater awareness, change of mindset and a whole-of-nation approach, we can end family violence and, with it, online harms from our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Thus, I am glad that both the White Paper and the Recommendations of the Taskforce on Family Violence are moving towards greater intervention, closer cooperation and rehabilitation efforts amongst all stakeholders.

sections.label: Women in workforce and leadership
sections.summary: More than 75% of women are in the workforce, over 50% of university graduates are women, 30% of parliamentarians, 13% of CEOs and 20% of board directors are women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More than 75% of women are in the workforce, more than 50% of University graduates are women, 30% of parliamentarians are women, 13% of CEOs are women and 20% of directors on boards are women.

sections.label: Inclusive workforce recommendations
sections.summary: The paper makes 12 recommendations at company, ecosystem, national and individual levels to create a more inclusive workforce and support women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The paper makes 12 recommendations at the company, ecosystem, national and individual level to help create a more inclusive workforce, advance women empowerment in the workplace and bolster women entrepreneurs.

sections.label: SBF report recommendations for businesses
sections.summary: SBF recommends businesses adopt TAFEP's Tripartite Standards for Work-Life Harmony, FWAs, and unpaid leave for unforeseen caregiving needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SBF has recommended in the report that businesses start by adopting TAFEP's Tripartite Standards for Work-Life Harmony; FWAs; and unpaid leave for unforeseen caregiving needs.

sections.label: Shell Singapore female leadership
sections.summary: In Shell Singapore, 39% of senior leaders based in Singapore are female and 37% of middle-management positions are held by females.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Shell Singapore, 39% of their senior leaders based in Singapore are female and 37% of middle-management positions are held by females.

sections.label: DBS and AKC diversity practices
sections.summary: DBS's diversity matrix shows women at 49% of workforce, 40% of SVPs, 29% of senior leadership and 20% of board; AKC gives extra leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: DBS' diversity matrix is also very encouraging, with women representing 49% of the workforce, 40% of SVPs, 29% of senior leadership and 20% on their board.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore SME, Absolute Kinetics Consultancy (AKC), gives its employees additional leave to support their child’s first day of school, enhanced paid childcare leave of two days on top of MOM-stipulated childcare leave as well as eldercare leave.

sections.label: Law on unacceptable workplace practices
sections.summary: The Government intends to write into law unacceptable practices, hoping the big stick is used as a last resort only.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government intends to write into law unacceptable practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hopefully, this big stick will be used as a last resort only and that our companies in Singapore, both the employers and the employees, will be able to work together to create a productive and respectful workplace culture with the increased awareness and training on managing biases and fair workplace practices.

sections.label: Women in senior management and boards
sections.summary: Women hold up to a-third of senior management positions; women directors in top 100 SGX-listed companies rose from 7.5% in 2013 to close to 20%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many women have been given opportunities to contribute and excel, rising up to a-third of the senior management positions in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have made improvements on the boards of the top 100 SGX-listed companies, from 7.5% of women directors in 2013, to close to 20% on 1 January 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Statutory Boards have also heeded the call for more balanced gender representation on boards and made good progress, improving from 23% in 2018, to 30% by the end 2021.

sections.label: Women on boards quotas
sections.summary: Singapore does not recommend quotas for women on boards, expecting 25% by 2025 and 30% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we do not recommend quotas for WOBs, as it can lead to tokenism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Like others have said, I think Singapore women, we can do it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are hopeful that with the momentum built and with the nine-year cap on independent directors rule change that has kicked in on 1 January, we should get to 25% by 2025 and 30% by 2030.

sections.label: Elective egg freezing concerns
sections.summary: The Government intends to legislate egg freezing for women aged 21 to 35, with frozen eggs usable only by married couples.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: After many years of debate on this issue, the Government has indicated an intended legislation to provide women aged 21 to 35 years, regardless of marital status, to preserve their eggs, and that only legally married couples can use their frozen eggs for procreation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: Will this put our women in a difficult position to have to choose to abdicate authentic womenhood and motherhood to technology because technology makes it possible for non-therapeutic egg freezing?

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: The cost of freezing and storing of human eggs is not insignificant, and one needs to add to it the cost of IVF treatment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: I worry that maternity will soon run the risk of being a commodity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: So, the time to act is now for our tripartite partners to urgently make the workplace work better for our women, especially the next generation, so that they can be supported to have fulfilling careers and have a life and a family as naturally as possible.

sections.label: Parenthood and egg freezing steps
sections.summary: In 2020 the age limit for IVF was removed and ART co-funding enhanced; elective egg freezing now extends to healthy women aged 21 to 35.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: In 2020, we took concrete steps to help women and couples fulfil their dream of parenthood with measures, such as removing the age limit for women undergoing IVF and enhancing the Government co-funding for assisted reproduction technology (ART) procedures.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Today, we are able to take another step forward with elective egg freezing for all healthy women aged 21 to 35.

sections.label: Egg freezing age limit
sections.summary: The speaker calls the age limit of 35 a pity and asks for more discussion to finetune the legislation for those aged 36 to 40.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Before they know it, they will be in their 30s and may be in the situations not unlike the stories I shared earlier.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I find it a huge pity that the age limit is set at 35 and that this policy is underserving a very important age segment, that is, those aged 36-40.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: If I may humbly ask, can we have more discussions on the age limit and finetune the legislation?

sections.label: Female fertility screening funding
sections.summary: Endometriosis and PCOS affect 20%-30% of women of reproductive age, and the speaker raises funding for female fertility screening.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Some common issues, such as endometriosis and PCOS, affect 20%-30% of women of reproductive age and these can cause infertility.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: On this topic of female fertility wellness, I would also like to bring up the possibility of funding for female fertility screening.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can implement a subsidised ladies' health check for women in their late 20s to early 30s or allow MediSave withdrawal for such screening and consultations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: When I first raised egg freezing in 2016, The Straits Times carried it as the top story in The Sunday Times.

sections.label: Women making informed choices
sections.summary: With more conversations, knowledge and counselling, women can shift mindsets and make sensible choices for themselves and their future.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: With more conversations, better knowledge and counselling, we, women, can shift mindsets, stay updated and make sensible choices for ourselves and our future.

sections.label: AIC caregiver referrals
sections.summary: AIC refers caregivers to help resources on a one-off, twice or thrice-off basis until issues are resolved and the case is closed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Presently, the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) refers caregivers to the appropriate help resources but the help would be once, twice or even thrice-off, until their issues are resolved and the case is considered closed.

sections.label: White Paper mid-term review
sections.summary: A question asks what targets are hoped to be seen at the mid-term review called for in the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As part of the White Paper is to call for a mid-term review, may I ask what do we hope to see at the mid-term review, in terms of targets being set?

sections.label: Subsidised places increase
sections.summary: The speaker says it would be helpful if the Ministry can increase the number of places at subsidised rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If the Ministry can increase the number of places at subsidised rates, it would be helpful.

sections.label: ElderShield reassessment waiver
sections.summary: A request is made to waive the ElderShield payouts' annual disability reassessment for those with permanent conditions, to relieve caregiver stress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In English): Finally, I would like to request a waiver of the ElderShield payouts' annual disability reassessment for those whose conditions are permanent, to relieve the stress on caregivers.

sections.label: Leave, WFH, unwed parents
sections.summary: The speaker proposes equalising paternity and maternity leave, legislating the right to request work from home, and extending tax and baby bonus benefits to single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, we should equalise paternity and maternity leave benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, we should legislate the right to request work from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And third, we should end the stigma against single unwed parents by extending to them the Parenthood Tax Rebate, the Working Mothers' Child Relief and the cash component of the Baby Bonus.

sections.label: Right to request WFH
sections.summary: The speaker proposes legislating employees' right to request work from home, which employers can turn down only for valid business-related reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second proposal today is that we legislate to give employees the right to request work from home, which employers can turn down only on the basis of valid business-related reasons.

sections.label: Right to work from home
sections.summary: The passage states fathers need continued access to work from home and that the right to work from home must be legislated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We will lose this momentum unless fathers continue to get access to work from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is clear – we need to legislate the right to work from home.

sections.label: Work from home and women
sections.summary: The passage states a right to work from home would reshape employer attitudes towards women and likely raise female labour force participation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Giving everyone the right to work from home will reshape the attitudes of employers towards women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It would also likely increase the female labour force participation rate, which, as Minister Tan See Leng has shared, is extremely low among women – only about 80% of women aged 25 to 64 are in the labour force.

sections.label: Policies excluding single unwed parents
sections.summary: The passage states government parenthood policies expressly exclude single unwed parents: Parenthood Tax Rebate, Working Mothers' Child Relief and Baby Bonus cash.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government has a whole suite of parenthood policies that expressly exclude single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These policies are the Parenthood Tax Rebate, the Working Mothers' Child Relief and the cash component of the Baby Bonus.

sections.label: Income of single unwed parents
sections.summary: The passage states young single unwed parents have a median monthly income of $600, among Singapore's lowest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Young single unwed parents have a median monthly income of just $600, among the lowest in Singapore.

sections.label: Stop excluding single unwed parents
sections.summary: The passage states single unwed parents should stop being excluded from the Parenthood Tax Rebate, Working Mothers' Child Relief and Baby Bonus cash.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, we need to stop excluding single unwed parents from the Parenthood Tax Rebate, the Working Mothers' Child Relief and the cash component of the Baby Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The White Paper is our commitment to a fairer and more inclusive Singapore.

sections.label: Gender equality progress
sections.summary: The passage states women's development is everybody's responsibility and Singapore must go further for gender equality progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I started this speech talking about how the development of women is something that all men and, indeed, all of us in Singapore can celebrate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is everybody's responsibility." We can and need to go further in order for Singapore's march towards gender equality to make true progress.

sections.label: Support for three vulnerable groups
sections.summary: The speech focuses on enhancing support for victims of online harm, those facing broken marriages, and low-income homemakers with dependants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For the purpose of today's speech, I will be focusing on enhancing support for three types of vulnerable groups: one, the victims of online harm; two, those who are feeling helpless as a result of a broken marriage; and three, homemakers with dependants in low-income families who are in need of a stable source of income.

sections.label: Legal clinic with social workers
sections.summary: The FJC legal clinic, supported by LSPBS, gives preliminary legal advice, and a pilot adds social workers for welfare issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: At present, the Family Justice Courts (FJC), through the support of LSPBS, runs a regular legal clinic to provide preliminary advice to individuals, regardless of their gender and nationality, on their legal rights when filing or defending proceedings in the FJC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I believe its effectiveness can be further enhanced by having a social worker participate in such sessions to assist those in need of other assistance, such as financial resources or employment opportunities, which are essential for divorcees, especially those homemakers and victims of domestic violence, to regain their confidence post-divorce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This arrangement is currently on trial under the pilot collaboration between LSPBS' Community Legal Clinics' collaboration with the Ang Mo Kio Family Service Centre where the lawyers advise on legal matters and the Family Service Centres (FSC) social workers assist to advise on welfare-related issues.

sections.label: Streamlining Family Justice Courts filing
sections.summary: Streamlining filing and a docket system would save time and costs, and MSF should work with FJC on measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Streamlining the filing process in the Family Justice Courts and having a docket system of all applications involving the same parties will save parties both time and costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I hope that MSF will work with the Family Justice Courts to introduce a series of measures to improve the process of filing applications, such as Personal Protection Orders as well as to enhance the enforcement of maintenance orders, in the Family Justice Courts.

sections.label: Alteraround project for homemakers
sections.summary: TaF.tc's Alteraround project trains women to earn income at home through alteration skills, training over 100 individuals since 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One inspiring example was shared by one of my Woodgrove community partners, the Textile and Fashion Industry Training Centre (TaF.tc), which currently runs the Alteraround project that aims to uplift the community of women who have either lost their jobs, retired or are stay-at-home mothers who wish to earn an income at home through an alteration skill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Since 2020, it has successfully trained more than 100 individuals and onboarded 17 seamstresses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Alteraround project is a small preview of what can be possible if more organisations are willing to come forward to collaborate with the community to empower homemakers with skills to be financially independent while having the flexibility to look after their families.

sections.label: More helpline operators at Montfort Care
sections.summary: MSF gave Montfort Care, which operates the NAVH, more resources, increasing call operators by 70%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To expand the capacity of the helpline to take more calls, MSF has provided more resources to social service agency Montfort Care, which operates the NAVH, increasing the number of operators to handle calls by 70%.

sections.label: Reporting abuse through new modes
sections.summary: By end-2022, witnesses and survivors can report violence via a web link and mobile application, with 16 taskforce recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: By end-2022, witnesses and survivors will be able to report violence or abuse with greater ease through new modes, such as a web link and mobile application.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: With the 16 recommendations from the Taskforce on Family Violence, we will act swiftly, strengthen deterrence and prevention, and rehabilitate perpetrators.

sections.label: Women's Charter consultation dates
sections.summary: Public consultations for related Women's Charter amendments start tomorrow and run until the end of April.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Public consultations for the related Women’s Charter amendments will start from tomorrow and run till the end of April.

sections.label: Family violence support centres
